title: Umbria Slips Back Under Two Euros
dek: Self-service Benzina in the green heart of Italy closed at €1.9984 on August 8th — its first sub-€2 reading in nine days — while diesel there runs well below the national mark.
body: Umbria's self-service Benzina came in at €1.9984 on August 8th, a hair under the national self-service average of €1.9994. The meaningful gap sits on the diesel pump: Gasolio self-service averaged €2.0865 in the region against €2.1090 nationally, leaving Umbrian drivers 2.25 cents per litre better off than the country as a whole. On a 50-litre fill that is a little over a euro — small in isolation, but it has held day after day through the tracked window. Full service tells the same story, €2.2336 regionally versus €2.2633 nationally, a 2.97-cent discount.

Direction matters as much as level, and both main fuels are falling. Benzina peaked at €2.0072 on August 4th and has declined on each of the four tracked days since, shedding 0.88 cents to drop back below the two-euro line for the first time since July 30th. Gasolio followed the same path, easing from €2.1004 to €2.0865 — a 1.39-cent decline. Metano ran the other way, climbing from €1.4336 to €1.4761 since August 5th. Behind those averages sits a small but conscientious network: 438 of Umbria's 481 registered stations filed prices, a 91.1% reporting rate that edges out the 90.6% recorded nationally (21,717 of 23,961) and keeps a compact region's figures genuinely representative.

Reading a single region at this resolution, every morning, is exactly the work a hand-maintained spreadsheet does not survive. Fuel Dashboard avoids the problem by rebuilding itself: it ingests the MIMIT open data, recomputes the national and regional aggregates, rotates the spotlight through all twenty regions on a fixed calendar cycle, and republishes the live site without anyone opening a file. The whole pipeline was built with Claude Code, and the payoff is that the daily effort goes into reading the numbers rather than assembling them.
pull_quote: Umbrian diesel runs 2.25 cents under the national average — and 438 of the region's 481 stations filed the prices to prove it.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight falls on Umbria, and it just dipped back under the two-euro line: self-service Benzina at €1.9984 on August 8th, its first sub-€2 reading since July 30th.

The more interesting number is diesel. Gasolio self-service averaged €2.0865 in Umbria against €2.1090 nationally, so drivers there pay 2.25 cents per litre less than the Italian average — and 2.97 cents less on full service. Both main fuels have now fallen four tracked days running, with Benzina off 0.88 cents from its August 4th peak and Gasolio down 1.39 cents. Metano moved the opposite way, climbing from €1.4336 to €1.4761 since August 5th. Reporting held up well too: 438 of Umbria's 481 registered stations filed prices, a 91.1% rate against 90.6% nationally.

All of this comes from Fuel Dashboard, a project tracking Italian fuel prices daily from MIMIT open data: national and regional averages across Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano, self and full service, with day-by-day history and a different region in the spotlight every morning. Have a look: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

The project is really an argument about method. Maintained by hand in Excel, a dashboard like this lasts about two weeks — download the CSV, clean it, recompute the averages, re-export the charts, then do it all again tomorrow. Instead the whole pipeline runs itself each morning: ingest, aggregate, regenerate, republish. I built it with Claude Code, and that is the honest case for AI coding tools — not typing code faster, but making a project sustainable that otherwise would never have been worth starting.
